rationale: The program is a C++ benchmark (Adobe-C++ simple_types_loop_invariant) dominated by simple-typed arithmetic inside loops where loop-invariant computation matters, so the profile is latency-sensitive and the static profile is empty, demanding a conservative, low-risk configuration. SUB gets high weights because arithmetic substitution is nearly free correctness-wise and directly obscures the invariant numeric expressions that dominate this code. IGV and ICALL are favored (low RuntimeCost/SizeCost weights, low risk) since data hiding and indirect calls add solid static-analysis resistance with minimal overhead. SPLIT is kept as a cheap enabler that increases block-level diversity and amplifies FLA/IBR. FLA is moderately weighted: it is the strongest structural defense but flattening hot loop bodies carries real runtime and correctness cost, so its RuntimeCost/CorrectnessRisk weights temper application to loop-heavy functions. BCF is effectively suppressed (high RuntimeCost and SizeCost weights) because bogus predicates inside tight loops waste cycles and bloat the binary with little added diversity beyond what SUB+FLA already provide. Overall the table steers selection toward low-cost semantic (SUB, IGV) and call/branch (ICALL, IBR) obfuscation while gating the expensive control-flow transforms against the loop-dominated hot paths.
